clue.text: Swimming in loch, lost skimpy apparel

indicators.note: swimming suggests letters moving about in the water, so the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bather in a Scottish loch has lost their scanty clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' rearranges the letters of IN LOCH plus LOST; 'lost' looks like the verb of the story but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments wrapped round the hips and nothing more are about as minimal as clothing gets.

clue.text: Illegal goods from source changing hands

indicators.note: hands are right and left, so the right-hand letter R is swapped for the left-hand L

parts.note: the root of something is its source or origin

explanation.surface: Smuggled goods passed on from the original supplier to a new owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' swaps R (right) for L (left) in ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunder or stolen property is goods taken illegally, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Prohibition popular with non-drinker hiding assorted cider

parts.note: something popular is in

indicators.note: the abstainer's letters conceal the scrambled drink between them

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a person who drinks no alcohol

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so the letters of cider are rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-liked teetotaller secretly keeps a supply of cider in defiance of a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assorted' scrambles the drink to ERDIC, and 'hiding' tucks that between the two letters for a teetotaller.
explanation.definitionFit: An interdict is a formal ban or order forbidding something.

clue.text: Thicket to get through carrying spades

indicators.note: the word for managing holds the suit letter inside it

parts.note: to cope is to manage or get through a difficulty
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A gardener must push through dense undergrowth with spades in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts S inside COPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small dense wood of trees or bushes, much like a thicket.

clue.text: First hole

explanation.surface: A golfer's opening shot: the first hole.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening game comes first, and an opening in a wall is a hole or gap.

clue.text: Tormented and chased around area

indicators.note: the pursued word wraps around the single letter for area

parts.note: to be hunted is to be pursued or chased

explanation.surface: A victim was tormented and chased all over the district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' places A inside HUNTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone haunted is troubled or plagued by persistent memories or fears.

clue.text: To paint without tips is impressive

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters, which are dropped here

parts.note: to depict something is to paint or portray it

explanation.surface: Painting a picture even without fine brush points is an impressive feat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without tips' removes the outer letters D and T from DEPICT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something epic is grand and heroic in scale, hence impressive.

clue.text: Container from lodge picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for lodge is taken as spoken

parts.note: to lodge a complaint or document is to file it

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves a container from the porters' lodge at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lodge' looks like a building, but it is the verb, as in lodging a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass bottle for medicine or perfume, a kind of container.

clue.text: On boat, served fancy old sugary food

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written on top of another comes before it
served up in a new form, so the two words are reshuffled

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
SS stands for steamship, a boat

explanation.surface: Aboard a ship, passengers were served an elaborate old-fashioned sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges FANCY OLD to CANDYFLO, and 'On' puts it above SS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun sugar on a stick, sold at fairs, is pure sugar confection.

clue.text: One manipulating crowd, mature Republican

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd of people
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A seasoned Republican politician skilfully manipulates the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur kneads and works the muscles, physically manipulating the body.

clue.text: Convenient work involving nothing too active, primarily

indicators.note: the work abbreviation surrounds the initial letters

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of each of the three preceding words

explanation.surface: A handy job requiring nothing very strenuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes N, T, A from 'nothing too active', which 'involving' puts inside OP.
explanation.definitionFit: On tap means available whenever wanted, like beer from a barrel tap, so readily convenient.

clue.text: Training duo at nice complex

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people in training together at a complicated site in Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges the letters of DUO AT NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling or instruction develops skills, which is what training does.

clue.text: Be present before expert is redeployed

indicators.note: redeployed means rearranged into new positions, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A specialist must be on site in advance before being moved to another post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redeployed' rearranges the letters of EXPERT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist earlier than something else is literally to be there beforehand.

clue.text: Some colossal tyrannosaurs like pretzels, perhaps

indicators.note: some of the following words, meaning a run of their letters is taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A few gigantic dinosaurs resemble pretzels in shape, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes letters from inside 'colossal tyrannosaurs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretzels are typically sprinkled with coarse salt crystals, making them salt-flavoured snacks.

clue.text: Activated the disc, now playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved around freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone started the record player, and the disc is now playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the letters of THE DISC NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning on a machine at its switch is starting it working.

clue.text: Wife in trouble, crying

parts.note: ailing means unwell or in difficulties

explanation.surface: A distressed wife in difficulty bursts into tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Wailing is loud mournful weeping, a form of crying out.

clue.text: One mountain restricting ways forward

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the mountain's two letters confine the methods word between them

parts.note: MT is the usual abbreviation for mount or mountain
modes are ways or methods

explanation.surface: A single mountain hems in the routes that lead onwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like part of 'ways forward' but means brazen; 'restricting' sets the ways word within the mountain's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward person is bold and presumptuous, lacking modesty or decorum.

clue.text: This compiler with G&T outside in control of fingers

indicators.note: the combined piece goes inside the control word

parts.note: a dial is a control knob

indicators.note: the drink's two letters sit on either side of the setter's pronoun

parts.note: gin and tonic, abbreviated G and T
the setter refers to themselves, giving I

explanation.surface: The setter, gin and tonic in hand, deftly works the controls with nimble fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts G and T round I to make GIT; 'in' places that inside DIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital relates to the digits, which are the fingers, hence pertaining to them.

clue.text: African thanks relative, acquiring Zulu a home to the north

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

indicators.note: the relative word takes the following letters inside it

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother, a relative
Z is Zulu in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: An African thanks a relation who has taken in a Zulu and found a home further north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' reads the home word upwards, giving NI; 'acquiring' puts Z, A and that inside the relative. Ta is casual British for thanks; nan is a grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tanzanian is a person from Tanzania, a country in East Africa.

clue.text: Representation of comet, it is symbolic

indicators.note: a representation presents things in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A depiction of a comet carries symbolic meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representation of' rearranges the letters of COMET IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem standing for a clan, so totemic means emblematic.

clue.text: Company with diverse board somewhere in Spain

indicators.note: diverse means varied, so the letters of board are mixed up

explanation.surface: A business with a varied board of directors is based in a Spanish location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverse' rearranges BOARD into RDOBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Córdoba is a city in Andalusia in southern Spain.

clue.text: Sprouts, they're often found in sofas

definitions.meaning: the coiled metal pieces inside upholstered furniture

explanation.surface: Brussels sprouts, as it happens, are often found down the back of the sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that springs up sprouts, and couch cushions contain coiled metal supports.

clue.text: Serious as soldiers

parts.note: as and since both mean because
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: As grave and solemn as soldiers are on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A sincere person is earnest and genuine, which is a sense of serious.

clue.text: Male with moisture around cut

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: around here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: dew is moisture deposited overnight

explanation.surface: A man surrounded by damp chopped something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reads the moisture word backwards; 'with' simply joins it to the male pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to chop with an axe, so hewed means cut.

clue.text: Bowls with produce, far end of potting shed

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so that letter is removed from the produce word

parts.note: goods are things produced, merchandise

indicators.note: the last letter of the word potting

explanation.surface: Bowls and other produce kept at the far end of the potting shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like the garden building but means discard: GOODS loses G, the last letter of 'potting'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the lawn game of bowls the balls are traditionally called woods, as they were made of lignum vitae.

clue.text: US farmer managed borders for hoodlum in prison

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, past tense ran

indicators.note: the outer letters go inside the prison word

parts.note: can is American slang for prison

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An American farmer was in charge of the boundaries for a gangster serving time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders for' takes H and M from 'hoodlum'; 'in' puts them inside CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large American livestock farm, and this is the man who runs one.

clue.text: Rises from helipad with troubles

parts.note: a helipad is marked with a large letter H
ills are troubles or misfortunes

explanation.surface: A helicopter takes off from a helipad despite its problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Helipads are painted with a big H for pilots to aim at.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise is an upward slope of ground, and so a hill is a rise.

clue.text: Mere mortal Hera struck infertile in the end

indicators.note: points to the final letter of each of the four preceding words

explanation.surface: A mere mortal was finally struck barren by the goddess Hera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like 'only', but it is a noun for a body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere is an old and poetic word for a pond or lake.

clue.text: Honey-bee circling cop's battered Scots delicacy

indicators.note: the bee word goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: a drone is a male honey-bee

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bee buzzes round a beaten-up police officer eating a Scottish treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' scrambles the officer's word to OPSC, which 'circling' puts inside the male bee. 'battered' also hints slyly at cookery.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch pancake, made by dropping batter onto a griddle, is a traditional Scottish teatime treat.

clue.text: Scratching sides, claw like a dog

indicators.note: scratching here means removing, so the outer letters of each word are struck off

explanation.surface: A dog scratching its flanks with a claw, just like dogs do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratching sides' strips CLAW to LA and LIKE to IK, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Laika was the Soviet dog launched into orbit aboard Sputnik 2 in 1957.

clue.text: Food from hospital lad rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a son is a boy or lad

explanation.surface: A boy in hospital refuses the meal he is given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reads H and SON backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food or a meal.

clue.text: Seems snake writhing around is logical

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It seems sensible that a snake should squirm about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhing around' rearranges SEEMS SNAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coherent and reasonable can be understood, which is the idiom's meaning.
